newsitem.title: TURKEY: CB CHIEF SAYS TURKEY NEEDS MEDIUM TERM PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: CB CHIEF SAYS TURKEY NEEDS MEDIUM TERM PROGRAMME.

text.p: Turkish central bank chairman Gazi Ercel said on Monday that the country was in need of a medium-term economic stability programme.

"I firmly believe that Turkish authorities, the Central Bank, Treasury, Ministry of Finance should at least design a...medium term programme and then address the kind of issues mainly aimed to reduce the inflation," Ercel told Reuters Financial Television in an interview at the world economic forum in Davos, Switzerland.

IMF officials are expected to visit Turkey by early March amid speculation that Ankara will implement a new IMF-sponsored economic programme. A plan put in place following a financial crisis in 1994 was abandoned after about 17 months.

"Of course we will exchange views on this subject," Ercel said. "But with the IMF or without the IMF, the Turkish authorities should at least address...inflation...also dealing with structural issues -- mainly broadening the tax base as well as dealing with the problems of the social security system."
In 1996, year-on-year consumer inflation was 79.8 percent. Ercel expects inflation to be in the 70s for 1997.
"I do believe that inflation will slightly decline through the middle part of the year," Ercel said.
